newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices off on data.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices off on data.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were flat to softer in early morning trade on Wednesday in the wake of the industrial output report.
In addition, the market was digesting a surge of competitive sales and secondary supply that hit the market during a strong rally on Tuesday.
"I think today's going to be spent sorting out. There was a little bit of new issue supply, especially competitive, and we were just innundated with bid wanted lists yesterday," a trader said.

However, most of the issues up for sale on Tuesday were not particularly desirable, and traders speculated that few bid-wanted lists would be seen on Wednesday, as customers prefer to sell when fixed-income markets are rising. But prices retreated after new statistics showed manufacturers were cranking up output, renewing fears that the Federal Reserve again might have to raise rates to restrain inflation.

March Industrial output rose 0.9 percent to 84.1 percent, the highest rate in two years. The gain exceeded the 0.6 percent increase forecast in a Reuters consensus survey of economists, who looked for the rate to firm to 83.6 percent.
Municipal bond sales on Wednesday were expected to total $850 million in 27 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings totaled $793 million in nine sales, with a $197 million Metropolitan Transit Authority deal through Bear, Stearns & Co., Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 18 sales totaling $57 million are on the schedule. A $22 million Oakland, Calif., at 1300 EDT is the largest.
Oregon's sale of $155 million of Certificate of Participations were priced with a top yield of 5.95 percent in 2024, according to Bear Stearns.
And Yuma, Ariz., Industrial Development Authority fetched 5.90 pcercent in 2017.
In debt futures, June Treasury bonds fell 19 ticks to 107-1/32, while the June municipal bonds lost 17 ticks to 112-2/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 161 ticks.
In the secondary market, Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey Revnues of January 2026, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.90 percent, NET, up three basis points.
Jefferson County, Alabama, Sewer Revenues of February 2027, which pay a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 96-5/8, level.
